pr_body: Closes #91614 | Before | After | | ------------- | ------------- | | | |
pr_comments:
> Does this also fix https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/90929?

This fixes a specific bug with vertex index mismatch that caused super sharp stripes when blending seams

I believe https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/91601 improved the situation with light leaks that are denoider-related

But there's still lots of room for improvement after our 2 fixes

These ones seem to be caused by the lightmap UVs being too small and packed too tightly, making the texture bleed onto its neighbours.

Edit: The lightmap looks like this, so leaks are bound to occur:
![lightmap](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/53150244/20e52e9d-4bee-4dbd-a395-753c1994a4cd)

> this doesn't appear to do much against the seams in the Global Illumination demo project

yeah because those aren't caused by wrong vertex indeces. There's more than one issue with lightmaps

If I had to guess those are most likely due to wrong UV offset calculation during seam blending

I was so happy that I found the bug, only to see now that you beat me to it. (Why doesn't Github notify me when there's a PR that would close an issue that I'm subscribed to?)

When the bug is fixed, the blending effect is so subtle that it's difficult to be sure whether it's working or just broken to the point where it does nothing. But there are actually some seams that look smoother with it.

The left is with seam blending disabled, the right is with the fix.

![blendseams-before-after](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/36154/7086a81f-38a3-4865-bb89-806554cdfda9)

While I was debugging, I noticed that the texels that are blended often don't perfectly line up with the actual seam. But that is a completely different issue.
@permelin I hope you'll beat me to fixing the bug that @Calinou pointed out because I'm not looking forward to fixing that 😂
Thanks! Great work tracking this down :1st_place_medal:

issue_context.title: LightmapGI: Stripes on curved surfaces
issue_context.body: ### Tested versions v4.3.dev6.official [89850d553] ### System information Godot v4.3.dev6 - macOS 14.4.1 - Vulkan (Forward+) - integrated Apple M1 Max - Apple M1 Max (10 Threads) ### Issue description I'm getting weird stripes when baking some geometry with LightmapGI and I can't get rid of them by tweaking any settings. I first reported this in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/90929 but I'm opening a separate issue for this as suggested by @lander-vr, because this seems to be a separate issue ### Steps to reproduce MRP ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [MRP_lightmap_stripes.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/15292112/MRP_lightmap_stripes.zip)
comments: As I said in the issue, how was the shape generated? Can you compare the result to when you do it from importing an OBJ?

These are really strange artifacts:
![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/31851431/27a43916-b38a-44e6-ae98-cc011b6e6c7e)

It looks like it's happening after denoising and dilation. Changing denoising parameters doesn't affect the shape, but does make it smoother. The dilated pixels themselves look normal to me.

After denoising:
![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/31851431/1e6239b0-2fdc-49f2-b1a0-9ef1f616b281)

Using a higher texel scale, those bands remain at the same width of 3 pixels.

> As I said in the issue, how was the shape generated? Can you compare the result to when you do it from importing an OBJ?

I imported gltf. Both gltf and the blend file that it came from are in the MRP

Tried exporting as OBJ, same result

> Can you compare the result to when you do it from importing an OBJ?

I don't think this is a UV issue that's carrying over into the raytracer, unless I misunderstood the issue you referenced in the other post. It seems to happen after all that somehow. Otherwise the dilated pixels would carry over the same values as those stripes, and the denoiser would at the very least make the shape of those stripes significantly less sharp.

I wonder if it's something that can trigger due to the nature of the concave shape and the rays probably hitting inside of the cylinder rather than outside. It's a bit odd it happens on the seams but it could explain why if it's being traced at the very edge of the seam. That's why I ask about the UV2, since it could be pushing it towards one of the edges perhaps since I only see one side of the seam being blurry. That hints that it's tracing from the right side on the pixel at one edge but not on the other edge.

I enabled debug_textures in lightmapper_rd. It seems to happen during the blendseams step.
This is the secondary light pass:
![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/31851431/c4c6b355-513f-41fd-8c43-b08c3f8a0bc2)

After blend seams:
![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/31851431/e6776030-1812-4825-86cb-07956306ffa3)

All other passes look completely fine to me.

> I wonder if it's something that can trigger due to the nature of the concave shape and the rays probably hitting inside of the cylinder rather than outside.

I don't think it's related to the shape, I'm fairly certain I've seen the same issue on one of my modular test scenes using planes in which it's also unaffected by denoiser settings:
![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/31851431/edf6f05b-236b-4b40-80ad-032cfab61b23)

> I enabled debug_textures in lightmapper_rd. It seems to happen during the blendseams step.

Interesting. I haven't really delved into the seams blend step yet so I can't give much info about that.
Also encountered it on beveled geometry, so it's not limited to concave shapes. Only sharp edges currently bake with no bugs. Updated the MRP to include this

Paging @reduz since he implemented the lightmapper (along with the blendseams step). Maybe he's got some ideas on what may be happening here. It would be nice to also hear what the blendseams step is trying to achieve.
To me the lightmaps seem to look fine after the secondary pass as is, so it might be worth exploring some bakes without the blendseams step. That said though, that may be a naive suggestion because I don't really understand blendseams.

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/78cce1954ddb6fefb90b33742215f304ec7b0b94/modules/lightmapper_rd/lm_blendseams.glsl#L102 This is what `lm_blendseams.glsl` draws in debug mode:
The sharp edge might mean that it's using a wrong uv offset when blending This is the part of the shader that blends lines: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/78cce1954ddb6fefb90b33742215f304ec7b0b94/modules/lightmapper_rd/lm_blendseams.glsl#L44-L70 These are the stages that blend seams in lines mode using that shader: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/78cce1954ddb6fefb90b33742215f304ec7b0b94/modules/lightmapper_rd/lightmapper_rd.cpp#L1929-L1939 https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/78cce1954ddb6fefb90b33742215f304ec7b0b94/modules/lightmapper_rd/lightmapper_rd.cpp#L1951-L1963

> It would be nice to also hear what the blendseams step is trying to achieve Without it you get... seams
BTW even when it's not doing the "same color for the entire stripe" artifact, it's still not doing a super great job at blending seams:
This is what it looks like when you don't blend with original color (if you swap this for `Vector3(0, 0, 1.0)`): https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/78cce1954ddb6fefb90b33742215f304ec7b0b94/modules/lightmapper_rd/lightmapper_rd.cpp#L1918
I also had some artifacts before where individual triangles of a mesh got outlined with stripes. So there's more than one problem to solve with seam blending

> BTW even when it's not doing the "same color for the entire stripe" artifact, it's still not doing a super great job at blending seams

It doesn't seem like the colour actually is the same for the whole stripe, that's an optical illusion due to the gradient :)
The main issue here is that the seam indexing is wrong, and some seams are back to front. Flipping the seam UV on the X axis fixes all the seams in those screenshots, but all the *other* seams that weren't previously broken become broken in the exact same way.

> It doesn't seem like the colour actually is the same for the whole stripe

Yeah you're right I just double checked at 100% opacity, they aren't single color
